neighbours.label: Contributing information so that an authority or researchers can learn (report side effects to the FDA, help doctors learn, help the agency track, tell us where): the verb or recipient of an information-giving request, vs the same topics with no information handed over
fire: Please report any suspected reaction to your local health authority right away.
Your answers will help scientists learn how sleep changes with age.
Help the park rangers track where the wolves travel each winter.
If you see a tagged turtle, tell us the date and the beach where you saw it.
Adverse events should be reported directly to the national safety agency.
Joining the registry helps researchers study why the condition runs in families.
Volunteers record bird sightings so the society can monitor population changes.
Let us know where you found this recipe so we can credit the source.
quiet: Please take any suspected reaction seriously and rest for a day.
Your sleep changes with age, and older adults often wake earlier.
The park rangers patrol the area where the wolves live each winter.
If you see a turtle on the beach, keep your distance and walk around it.
Adverse events are rare and usually disappear within a few days.
The condition runs in families and often appears in childhood.
Volunteers feed the birds every morning in the society's garden.
This recipe uses fresh basil and a little lemon juice.

predictions: 'report ... to', 'help X learn/track/study', 'tell us' reach 0.35-1.0; sentences about the same side effects, animals or diseases without an information request stay under 0.1.
notes: Card: peaks on ' us' (Please tell us), ' improve', ' to' (report to FDA), ' study', ' learn', ' track', ' reported', ' knowledge', also log-file writes in code. Probe: 'help doctors learn' 0.962, 'report side effects to the FDA' 0.810, 'help ... track' 0.525, 'tell us where' 0.353; 'notice side effects' 0.014, bears 0.021, 'Doctors know' 0.069, 'tell your friends about our bakery' 0.065.
